items.title: Marvel Snap Axis Inversion Season: All New Cards Revealed
Top 10 Games Featuring The Wolverine
items.summary: Discover the 10 best Wolverine video games to play before Marvel’s Wolverine drops. From retro beat 'em ups to action RPGs.
items.content:
With Marvel’s Wolverine on the horizon, we can’t help but be excited about slipping into some lovely yellow lycra and getting short, hairy, and angry. If you’re looking to slash through some enemies with everyone’s favourite berserker, we’ve got you covered.

While there aren’t tons of games dedicated solely to Logan, there are plenty of amazing titles featuring him. Here is our definitive top ten list of the best Wolverine video games to play right now.

Look, we know the film wasn’t especially good, but the movie tie-in video game was an absolute banger. It was one of the earliest titles where you could truly rip enemies to shreds in authentic Wolverine style, and the hack-and-slash action still holds up today. It’s a little rough graphically—having originally launched in 2009—but it remains a blast to play.

Marvel’s take on the hero shooter genre is a fantastic time for anyone who doesn’t mind being assaulted by sheer visual scale. Wolverine serves as a furious melee disruptor in the roster. Despite getting up close and personal, he can hold his own very easily thanks to some clever character design choices. It’s an excellent multiplayer game if you want fast-paced competitive action.

A triumphant return to the iconic co-op action RPG style of yore, Marvel Ultimate Alliance 3: The Black Order lets you and your team fight through hordes of Marvel baddies. It’s a wonderfully chaotic game that’s perfect for friends and families looking for something a little more “brain-off, fun-up.”

With newer fighting games missing the mark for some fans, now is an amazing time to revisit Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3 . This legendary crossover fighter pits classic Capcom icons against a huge roster of Marvel heroes, letting them battle to the death in fast-paced 3v3 combat. Grabbing the Ultimate edition nets you loads of content across various game modes—plus the chance to test your skills online.

Marvel’s Midnight Suns is simply brilliant. This tactical turn-based RPG puts you in the boots of an ancient demon slayer teaming up with iconic Marvel characters to fight off supernatural horrors. Beyond its incredibly deep deck-building mechanics, it features an amazing story packed with memorable hero interactions.

This counts, right? Wolverine is a card, after all! While the initial launch hype has settled, playing a few quick rounds of Marvel Snap is still one of the best ways to kill time between daily tasks—or while on the toilet. It’s a simple yet deeply engaging card game where you can lead Logan and other Marvel heroes to victory.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion brings back classic beat ’em up action with retro sensibilities and modern polish. You can choose from fifteen different playable heroes and team up with friends to smash through alien threats. With its authentic arcade feel, it stands out as one of the best modern co-op brawlers available.

Lego Marvel Super Heroes stems from the golden era of Lego gaming—where every title felt familiar yet endlessly entertaining. Even years after its release, the charming visual style hasn’t aged a bit, and the comedic writing is sublime. It’s the ultimate option for gaming with younger players, offering pure good vibes despite the cosmic-level threats.

This retro bundle collects a massive lineup of 90s Marvel classics, letting you step into the shoes of various iconic heroes—Wolverine included. As a recent release, it’s a fantastic retro anthology for anyone looking to experience how comic book games used to feel during the arcade era.

While we haven’t played it yet, early looks are stunning. Given Insomniac Games’ incredible track record with the Marvel’s Spider-Man series, we have high expectations for Logan’s standalone adventure. Set within the same shared universe as Spider-Man, it promises a rich narrative payoff for fans following Insomniac’s Marvel universe.

Jason likes to focus on roguelikes and co-op games; in a dream world he'd make a living writing about Dark Souls. As well as being a writer he also does personal training and accounting and can occasionally be seen on other people's streams. Being a big fan of fluffy things means he has two cats, both of whom refuse to let him sleep, but at least they are cute.

Open a web ticket to contact our Customer Support team.

items.summary: Fans have been asking for a Draft Mode and Second Dinner delivers with an offering fits the 12-card deck “Marvel Snap” game

items.title: Marvel Snap's Draft mode is a limited-time breath of fresh air
items.content:
Feature Preview Modojo @ Shacknews Marvel Snap's Draft mode is a limited-time breath of fresh air Marvel Snap's upcoming Draft mode is such a refreshing shift from the meta that you'll wish it could stay around longer.

The announcement of the August 2026 season of Marvel Snap was an exciting one for a few reasons. First, it marked the return of Second Dinner co-founder Ben Brode to the reveal videos after several months away. Second, Brode teased a major new reveal for Marvel Snap. That reveal is a limited-time game mode called Draft. Draft shakes up the standard Marvel Snap formula in some big ways. I recently had a chance to try it out and I walked away hoping that Second Dinner would consider making Draft a more permanent mode.

Marvel Snap's Draft mode tasks players with putting together a set of ten cards, which will expand to a full 12-card deck over the course of a run. Players begin by selecting a Starter Set, all of which follow an archetype like Swarm, Ramp, or Control. One of the Starter Set cards will appear front-and-center, appearing as the lead card to build around. For my session, I wouldn't be a toxic Snap player if I didn't select Shang-Chi as soon as the opportunity presented itself. This Shang-Chi control set was accompanied by Star-Lord and The Punisher. While I didn't think those cards went together, it was the actual draft portion where I would get to flesh out this deck.

The actual draft portion presents players with three cards to select from, continuing on until a ten-card deck has been assembled. In many cases, players will select from vanilla versions of cards, which have been separated into rarities. It'll be tempting to pass up cards with Epic and Legendary rarities, especially during rounds where every selection features a special buff. That buff could include a reduced Cost, an increased Power stat, or a bonus Quickdraw effect, just to name a few possibilities.

Decks assembled during a Draft will not follow the typical Marvel Snap meta. For many players, that's going to be the new mode's most alluring feature. Those who have grown tired of seeing whatever deck is dominating Untapped are, more often than not, going to see something wildly different. This is a mode that's all about testing a player's deck-building skills with whatever limited selections are available to them. After each game, players will get to upgrade their deck in different ways. That'll include picking cards to fill the deck to the usual 12-card amount, as well as picking Augments for their existing cards. Once I was presented a double On Reveal Augment option for my Shang-Chi, I was ready to live up to my most toxic potential.

The cream of the crop will ride their choices to five wins before accruing two losses, with an option to use a Respawn token to stay alive after the second loss. Once the run ends, the player will receive a slew of in-game rewards. The amount of goodies that I got for finishing with five wins was more than I expected. I received Bits for the Draft shop, XP for the Event Pass (which will operate similarly to Event Passes for other game modes), a Mystery Variant, Boosters, and another Draft ticket to play again. Just like other limited-time modes like Grand Arena, players will have a set number of Draft tickets, but that number will refresh over time.

As somebody who has admittedly gone through the motions with Marvel Snap's standard game mode, Draft mode put an extra spring in my step. The game felt fresh again. The only disappointment is knowing that it'll only be around for a limited time. This is something I want to see as a permanent feature, a mode that could complement standard play similar to what Arena does for Hearthstone , an idea that the Second Dinner team should be fairly familiar with.

Marvel Snap's Draft mode will go live later today and will stay active until September 8. Enjoy while it's around, but even after it's gone, expect it to stay in the LTM rotation, like High Voltage and Sanctum Showdown before it.

This preview is based on a Steam beta branch build provided by the developers.

items.title: MARVEL SNAP DRAFT
items.summary: BUILD! BUFF! BATTLE! The most requested mode in MARVEL SNAP history has arrived. Draft drops you into a brand-new way to build: no collection, no pre-made decks, just you, a fresh set of cards, and the Augments to turn them into something w
items.content:
BUILD! BUFF! BATTLE!

The most requested mode in MARVEL SNAP history has arrived. Draft drops you into a brand-new way to build: no collection, no pre-made decks, just you, a fresh set of cards, and the Augments to turn them into something wild. Here is everything you need to know before your first run.

WHAT IS DRAFT?

It's MARVEL SNAP meets draft style deck building, meets roguelike style upgrades! MARVEL SNAP Draft does not depend on your collection - you can draft from any available cards in the mode. Then, you get to flex your skills and adjust on the fly with Augments that add cool abilities, or leverage Stat Boosts that help you fight for priority.

WHY PLAY DRAFT?

Big Potential: Decks in Draft have more potential than ever, melding the excitement of a limited environment with the high-power potential of a roguelike. Always Fresh: Augments allow you to add abilities to cards to create unique abilities you've never seen in a normal SNAP game! Level Playing Field: Everyone can enjoy Draft whether you've been playing for years or just started yesterday, no collection required.

HOW DO YOU PLAY DRAFT?

Build your deck, take it to battle, secure two out of three Locations after turn 6, and DOMINATE the Draft on your way to 5 wins. It starts with your choice of 3 core stacks of cards. Pick between them to set the foundation of your deck. Add on to your core by drafting one of three cards until you fill out your initial 10 card deck. After each game, you'll get a chance to add to your deck or buff your cards with Augments. You can have a Black Panther with an additional doubling of Power, or a Wolverine that also destroys another card to get stronger! Sounds wild, right? Each win will be rewarded, but getting to 5 wins will grant you an additional entry ticket, a once per day bonus of a PMV, and other awesome rewards. Watch out though, 2 losses and it's back to the drafting board.

WHAT ARE AUGMENTS?

Augments are abilities you can apply to cards that add additional effects. If you're lucky, you'll even get an opportunity to Draft cards straight into your deck with Augments. They let you make super strong plays, and you can even put multiple Augments on the same card!

WHAT ARE STAT BOOSTS?

Unlike Augments, which fundamentally alter the nature of a card beyond just the numbers on it, Stat Boosts make cards cheaper or stronger. Sometimes, you'll get a Vision that costs 4, or has 11 power - that's a Stat Boost in action!

HOW LONG WILL MARVEL SNAP DRAFT BE HERE?

Draft will be available through September 8th at server reset. The shop will remain open for an additional 48 hours after the mode has ended to ensure there is ample time to maximize your currency. If you can't get enough Draft, be on the lookout for surveys where you'll get to tell us about your experience (and maybe even encourage the team to bring it back super fast).

DRAFT LOGIN REWARDS

We've already announced the first 3 decks in our Fractured Frontier Blog, but now it's time to celebrate Draft by announcing 2 MORE decks! A Mister Negative deck that inverts costs to make wild combos, and a Victoria Hand deck that boosts your created cards. That's right, we're putting 5 complete decks in login bonuses that are available to EVERYONE. Yes, everyone. Login ➡ get rewarded. This will happen over two different login events covering Aug 24 - Sep 6th, and Sep 7th - Sep 28th.

MINI-EVENTS FOR DRAFT AND RANKED!

Being rewarded for playing feels good. Grabbing a free Series 5 Collector's pack for playing feels even better! Tune in for multiple new Mini-Events to complete in both Draft and Ranked matches. These Mini Events will be available for 2 days. Here's the schedule of events and their rewards.

items.title: MARVEL SNAP Draft Hands-On Preview – Here For A Good Time
items.summary: MARVEL SNAP’s new Draft Mode is a refreshing addition, but it would likely take much more to revitalize the game as a whole.
items.content:
Released on mobile and PC (early access) in the fall of 2022, MARVEL SNAP is a digital collectible card game and the brainchild of former Hearthstone game director Ben Brode , and Second Dinner, the studio he founded after leaving Blizzard. Upon its release, MARVEL SNAP proved not only to be a critical darling, winning Best Mobile Game at The Game Awards in 2022, but also immensely popular with players, becoming the top-grossing digital trading card game by September 2023, according to Forbes .

I, myself, was completely enamoured with it and played it roughly every day, racking up countless hours on mobile and around 38 hours on Steam. Furthermore, in December 2022, I wrote about the best decks to try – that article is long outdated, of course, but for a taste of what players were concocting at the time, you may find it here .

However, a few years on, MARVEL SNAP finds itself, for a myriad of reasons , in the difficult situation of having lost 75% of its revenue in 2025 and, presumably, a significant chunk of its player base, too. In an effort to revitalise the game, Second Dinner is finally adding a game mode that fans have been asking for ever since launch: Draft. Like in many other card games, digital or otherwise, MARVEL SNAP ’s Draft mode will have players build temporary decks from random selections of cards.

Unlike other card games, though, there is also a roguelike element at play here, with cards being able to be “augmented” after each round. Depending on the buffs available, Black Panther, for example, can have his power doubled a second time, which can be extremely valuable. Because of this, having good synergy not just between the cards themselves but the augments, as well, becomes crucial to securing a win. Each individual win will be rewarded, but getting to 5 wins will grant an additional Draft ticket alongside currency rewards. Drafts can go on for a maximum of 6 rounds, with players allowed to lose just the single time before proceedings come to a close.

Earlier this month, courtesy of the MARVEL SNAP developers, I was invited to a preview session in which they told me about what it took for them to bring Draft to their game, culminating in me getting some hands-on time with this new game mode. From the get-go, the team at Second Dinner mentioned that Draft is probably the most requested feature and that they’ve wanted to implement it in the game for a long time.

Because of the way that MARVEL SNAP is put together, specifically with regard to card rarity, they spoke about how difficult it was to implement the mode but that, ultimately, they are incredibly confident in this latest iteration of Draft, which has been in the works for the past year or so. Their hope is that Draft becomes a mainstay for both returning and perhaps especially new players, since no pre-existing card collection is needed to get the most out of it.

Unfortunately, Draft itself isn’t here to stay, as it will only be a limited game mode in MARVEL SNAP , running from the 24th of August at noon PT until the 7th of September at noon PT. This is disappointing, definitely, but my impression is that the team is more than open to bringing it back, potentially with a new pool of cards, if player reception is positive.

For what it’s worth, based on my time playing and winning 5 rounds of Draft, they absolutely should, as this is a good game mode which, with a bit more love and polish, could become one of the main reasons players are picking up MARVEL SNAP in the first place.

My hope is that things work out and that Draft makes a tangible impact on MARVEL SNAP , but if it only runs for the limited period specified above, my fear is that it won’t get the time to do so. I certainly won’t be back if Draft is here for a good time, not a long time.

Image: Second Dinner Marvel SNAP Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap After years of clamoring from its player base, Marvel Snap will finally get a Draft mode on Aug. 24.

Draft will be a limited-time game mode that will heavily modify the standard gameplay loops of the Marvel Comics-inspired collectible card game. An exclusive preview and interview with GameSpot detailed what Marvel Snap players can expect from Draft. Matches begin with players choosing a starter set that gives them three cards that fit different deck archetypes like destroy, ramp, move, or ongoing.

Players then draft seven more cards, which have modified cost or power stats specific to this mode or have "augments" that give them additional abilities. From there, players have to win five rounds of Draft to claim victory, building up their deck with two more cards (and more augments) over time.

Developer Sam Stoddard explained that the radical gameplay changes required for Draft are part of the reason it took so long for Second Dinner to make the mode. That's also why it's starting as a limited-time game mode and not a whole new permanent part of the game.

"Snap has a much lower number of cards, you have very small decks, so even the amount of variance you get isn’t super high, as well as the synergy is very high. There’s all these things that were really working against it, and it’s part of why it took so long to eventually get to a place where we were really happy with what we had as an offering," Stoddard explained to GameSpot. "And so part of the LTGM thing is that we have a lot of known unknowns right now. I enjoy the mode a lot, but I designed it. I’ve talked to a lot of other people who enjoy it, but we definitely need to really stress test it with a much larger group of people."

While there might be some issues that still need to be worked out, Draft mode is one of the most exciting updates for the game since its 2022 launch. Nearly four years and several controversies later , Marvel Snap maintains a passionate community and player base, with the game still receiving a brand-new card every single week. It's my favorite mobile game, and one of my favorite Marvel games in general, so I'm very happy to see the mode finally arrive.

Draft will arrive in the Android, iOS, and Windows PC versions of Marvel Snap on Aug. 24. As for when it'll return once this initial event concludes, Stoddard says that's something Second Dinner "will be trying to figure out from all that data," but that it won't "be too long before it comes back because we definitely have a lot of things that we want to try out."

Gunslingers stalk the wasteland and every dusty crossroads hides new cards, locations, and events. New faces (and a few old ones) are drawing steel across the roster, two new locations are riding onto the map, and a full calendar of events guarantees there's always another showdown waiting. NEW KEYWORD: QUICKDRAW

Quickdraw: These effects are active the first turn you draw them. (Next turn if cards are already revealing.) Say hello to Quickdraw, a new keyword that rewards drawing the right card at the right time. A card's Quickdraw effect becomes active on the turn you draw it, or on the following turn if cards have already started revealing, giving every draw the potential to change your plans. Example: Draw Psylocke Fractured Frontier at the perfect moment to discount your entire hand, or let Jane Foster Fractured Frontier judge the worthy a second time. Thanos Fractured Frontier takes the mechanic even further, giving all your cards Quickdraw and loading another Infinity Shot whenever you draw them, opening the door to explosive turns and new deck-building strategies.

MINI-EVENTS!

Something NEW is stirring up dust across the frontier, including SIX more Mini-Events this season to help you load up and get ready for your next showdown. Here's how they work. First, a Mini-Event appears in-game with a mission-level achievement (think Collect XP, Hyper Cube Rush, and more). Second, complete the requirements to snag your reward and saddle up for the next one. To celebrate the launch of Mini-Events, our first reward will be a Collector's Series 5 SNAP Pack! Out on the Fractured Frontier, you gotta be fast! These Mini-Events will only be around for a couple of days before they're gone, so check in often. When one appears, don't let it ride off without you!

items.title: ‘Marvel Snap’ slowly levelling up: three upgrades and three features that need work
items.summary: Marvel Snap has had an uneven year. It started strong with a season focused on dragons and a second volume of Guardians of the Galaxy. Second Dinner introduced powerful cards that overwhelmed players with power and needed tweaking.
items.content:
Marvel Snap has had an uneven year. It started strong with a season focused on dragons and a second volume of Guardians of the Galaxy. Second Dinner introduced powerful cards that overwhelmed players with power and needed tweaking.

The next two months, March and April, introduced a new quest-like mechanic called Objectives. The cards weren’t overly impressive, and the new keyword was bland because of its ho-hum effects and how it worked. They were also thematically too close to each other. It was two months of offerings that mostly felt skippable, well, except for Isca the Unbeaten and Techno-Organic Virus.

Since then, Marvel Snap has found its groove, introducing compelling cards that augmented some archetypes, while adding new ones. Along the way, Second Dinner has also found a good rhythm with limited-time game modes that spiced up the weekend and offered compelling rewards such as Ozymandias and Mother Askani.

After the stumble, the team also added a slew of improvements that have made the overall game better. Here are three new features that have made the game better, and three that need a major overhaul.

1. Wild boosters – One of the key parts of Marvel Snap is upgrading cards. It’s how players improve their looks for bragging rights, while also raising the Collection Levels in order to get Collector’s Reserve boxes, credits, boosters and the all-important Collector’s Tokens.

The problem with this system is that sometimes players had a card they liked or one they were trying to upgrade, but they didn’t have the Booster for it. They lacked the required number to raise a card to a new level. Second Dinner fixed this by giving players Wild Boosters, which they can use on any cards. It’s a godsend for players who are close to a card upgrade or want to try for a special Finish or Flare to make their card look extra impressive.

2. Split rerolls – Another quality-of-life improvement comes when players reach a card’s Infinite level. That’s when they’re granted a new Finish and Flare. In the past, if players had a bad result, they were stuck with it. Now, Second Dinner gives players a chance at one free reroll of either Finish or Flare.

To gain this option, a card must hit level 10, meaning that players have upgraded it enough times or they have acquired enough variants to raise it to that level. Once there, each time players hit Infinite with a card, they have a chance to switch up the Flare and Finish if they don’t like it. It’s another chance to get a coveted Ink finish or Krackle.

3. Hyper cube rush – A running joke around Marvel Snap has been the concept of “Dadfinite.” Busy adults don’t have the time to grind to Infinite, so for them, reaching level 90 is the best they can do. Second Dinner saw that barrier and offered a path to the game’s highest ranks through this recently introduced feature.

It gives bonus cubes several times a season, boosting players’ journey toward their Infinite goal. It makes the highest ranks attainable for players who are skilful but don’t have enough time to deal with the matches needed to hit the top tier.

Star Lord, Master of the Sun, highlights the cards coming in the new season of Marvel Snap . Although Marvel Snap has made strides, it still needs to work in these areas:

1. Series drop – It’s been more than a year since Second Dinner lowered the tiers for cards. For veterans whose collection is near complete, that doesn’t mean much, but for newcomers entering the game, it has been a burden.

Older cards such as Jeff the Baby Land Shark are still at the most expensive Series 5 status. Marvel Snap is long overdue to make key cards such as Cosmic Ghost Rider, Red Guardian, Khonshu and Sam Wilson Captain America more accessible.

2. Alliance – Adding a group component to Marvel Snap was a smart move, but Second Dinner hasn’t updated it in a while. The feature is a way to encourage players to try new decks and go out of their comfort zone with bounties. Unfortunately, the End of Week Rewards haven’t been great since Premium Mystery Packs were removed.

It is easy to redeem Marvel Snap codes. All you have to do is:

Marvel Snap codes are used to get rewards in the game. Most of these are cosmetic, such as new borders for cards or variant images. However, there are some that give Credits and Boosters, which can help you get powerful new cards for your deck.

Marvel Snap codes are usually announced via developer Second Dinner’s social media channels. This often happens when new Marvel movies are released, such as Spider-Man: Brand New Day, or when new in-game events take place. It is worth following Second Dinner to be sure you’re always the first to find out about new Marvel Snap codes.

In 2025, Marvel Snap was temporarily banned in the US. This wasn’t due to any of the content in the game, however. Instead, it was because of where the game was developed. Nuverse, the publisher of Marvel Snap, is owned by ByteDance, the same Chinese company that owns the social media platform TikTok. In January 2025, the Republican-controlled US government banned internet traffic from ByteDance in the US, which inadvertently caused Marvel Snap to go down. Access was restored a few days later.

    FEATURED SETS

    Featured Sets deliver curated collections of cards and variants with smaller reward pools so you can target specific themes.

    Chibi Pack available June 4–8.

    Who will win the next Golden Gauntlet Qualifier? Join the competition, or tune in for the live broadcast on June 6th to watch an incredible display of strategy and skill. The Champion's deck will be featured in the Card Shop, so you can play what the champions play! Look out for this incredible opportunity from June 11–15 at server reset.

    Discard Variant Pack available June 25–29.

    Now get out there, soak up the sun, and make the most of Marvel Beach Bash. We can't wait to see what decks you build, what plays you discover, and what big beach-day moments you share with us. And don't forget your sunscreen!

Hell's Kitchen is under siege. Who's side are you on? The dark and broody Shadowlands Daredevil… or Wilson Fisk doing his best good guy impersonation?

Let's take a quick look at the incredible web shop bonus, then dive into our newest season!

WEB SHOP BONUS

Purchase the Premium or Super Premium Season Pass on shop.marvelsnap.com and unlock AWESOME bonuses, including a Series 5 SNAP Pack and 3 Red Matte Card Borders.

To ensure you get your rewards:

  • Log in to the game during the new season

    [/*]

  • Log into the Web Shop and purchase the Premium or Super Premium Pass

    [/*]

  • Reload your SNAP client and claim your new rewards

    [/*]

    Upgrading from Premium → Super Premium will NOT trigger the bonus. You must purchase the pass directly through the Web Shop.

    TWITCH DROPS

    This season we're bringing you two Twitch Drops campaigns. Drops are available May 19–21 during Sanctum Showdown Surge, and May 28–30 during Team Clash!

    If you haven't linked your account, visit https://twitch.marvelsnap.com/ to get set up. If your button still says "link" but you're earning progress, you can ignore the message and proceed as normal.

    Watch 2 hours to earn: 155 Random Boosters

    Watch 4 hours to earn: Premium Mystery Border

    Watch 6 hours to earn: Premium Mystery Variant

    SEASON PASS

    Purchase the Premium Season Pass and command Shadowlands Daredevil, or go Super Premium to add Wilson Fisk to your roster with an exclusive variant from Viktor Farro.

                           SHADOWLANDS DAREDEVIL

                            PREMIUM PASS / SERIES 5

                                        On Reveal: Shuffle in 3 Demons.

                     When you draw a card with 6 or more Power, +2 Power.

                                        WILSON FISK                     

                      SUPER PREMIUM PASS / SERIES 5

                   Costs 3 if you have the highest Power among cards in play.

    NEW CHARACTERS!

                                                           SERIES 5

          On Reveal: Give one of your 1, 2, and 3-Cost characters +2 Power each.

                                                           SERIES 5

                           When drawn, mark one of your empty locations.                         Objective: Win that location → +1 Max Energy.

                                                           SERIES 5

                              Ongoing: +3 Power for each location where

                                 one of your cards has been destroyed.

                                                           SERIES 5

                          On Reveal: Afflict an enemy card with -2 Power.

              Repeat on a different enemy for each of your unspent Energy.

                                       LIMITED TIME EVENT / SERIES 4

          You can only play this where an enemy is afflicted with negative Power.

                                       LIMITED TIME EVENT / SERIES 4

                                 On Reveal: Give the next card you play

                                       Power equal to this card's Power.

    NEW TO SNAP PACKS

    May 9: Askani'Son – Seasonal Series 4

    May 23: Mother Askani – Seasonal Series 4

    NEW LOCATIONS

    Josie's Bar: Playing 2 cards here in a turn reveals them with +2 Power.

    Island Prison: Cards here can't move.

    LIMITED TIME GAME MODES

    For more information on upcoming game modes and more, be sure to join our Discord! discord.gg/marvelsnap

    We're introducing a new citrus flavored twist on our favorite game of location domination! The new rules will have you surging around the world as you start with 4 energy and 4 cards in hand. But it's not just energy, you earn points way faster! This mode offers a total potential of 4 points on turn 1, 7 points on turn 2, and 9 points by turn 3! Play and progress on the reward track to unlock the new Series 4 card, Ikari.

    Surge is available May 14–21. The shop will remain open for an additional 48 hours.

    Pick a side and take on the competition in this mode that rewards playing favorites. Progress to unlock the new Series 4 card, Stick.

    Team Clash is available May 28 – June 3. The shop will remain open for an additional 48 hours.

    NEW ALBUMS

    Get all new Variants, Emotes, and rewards by completing new albums!

    Iban Coello's On the Grind (May 12)

    Album Variants: Khonshu, The Blob, Agent Venom, Agent Coulson, Super Skrull, Starbrand, Gambit, Scream, Scorn, Arishem Collect 3: Punisher War Machine Angry Emote Collect 6: 3 Premium Mystery Borders Collect 8: 4000 Collector's Tokens Collect 10: Shou Lao Variant

    Envar Painted Lineart (May 26)

    Album Variants: Professor X, Uatu, Joaquin Torres, Werewolf By Night, Diamondback, Cobra, Wiccan, Stature, X-23 Collect 3: Uatu "What" Emote Collect 5: 6 Cosmic Gold Borders Collect 7: White Tiger Variant Collect 9: Scarlet Spider Variant

    SHOP TAKEOVERS

    Iban Coello Variants available May 12–13.

    Envar Painted Lineart Variants available May 26–27.

    FEATURED SETS

    Featured Sets deliver curated collections of cards and variants with smaller reward pools so you can target specific themes.

    Make your deck Iron-clad with this themed set featuring Hulkbuster, Ironheart, Iron Lad, Iron Patriot, Rescue, War Machine, and of course… Iron Man! Available May 14–18.

     

    The Man Without Fear takes center stage. Available May 21–25.

     

    Channel your inner adventurer with fantasy-themed variants. Available May 28 – June 1.

     

    Now get out there, take control of Hell's Kitchen, and make Daredevil proud. See you on the ladder!

items.content:
That's right, MARVEL SNAP is participating in the Steam Deckbuilders Fest from May 4-11. To celebrate, we're launching new bundles and featuring content from the MARVEL SNAP Content Creator program the whole week!

Whether you're just getting started or looking to supercharge a specific playstyle, there's a bundle built for you. If this IS your first time here, welcome!

Here's the TLDR: The game is free to play, and cards can be unlocked by progressing your Collection Level. Progression is made when you upgrade the cosmetics of your cards which requires Boosters and Credits. If you like to go fast, these bundles will speed up your progression. If you want to jump straight into a specific archetype, these bundles will help you make that happen.

STEAM SPECIAL: ENTRY PACK

The most accessible offer in the lineup, the Entry Pack is a perfect choice for new players. At full price, this would still be one of the best deals out there. With an extra 40% off, this is going to be hard to beat.

  • Doctor Doom - Base Card

    [/*]

  • Doctor Doom - Pior Oberson Variant

    [/*]

  • 310 Doctor Doom Boosters

    [/*]

  • 1,500 Gold

    [/*]

ARCHETYPES? WHAT SHOULD I GET?

If you're just getting started, think about the play style that you typically have fun with. Destroy is for the player that believes a little self sacrifice is worth the explosive value. Discard gives you control of the grave yard and lets you reanimate on command. On Reveal is for the big chain combo player that loves to feel unstoppable. Ready to jump in?

DESTROY STARTER PACK

Smash, Crash, and Chomp. This archetype lets you Destroy cards on both sides of the battlefield to stack power and keep your opponents on edge. This bundle is the powder keg that helps you build the explosive play lines.
